title: EEG-cleanse: an automated pipeline for cleaning electroencephalography recordings during full-body movement
author: Rico-Olarte, Eskofier, et al.
materials: Real-World Validation: tested in real human interaction.
Hardware-Independent and Flexible: requires no auxiliary sensors

steps.title: Load raw OpenBCI recordings
steps.instruction: Import the 308 EEG recordings collected with OpenBCI hardware from 14 participants; each recording contains a still‑baseline (GT) and an active‑movement (MVMT) stage. Exclude the two recordings with integrity issues, leaving 306 sessions (82 GT and 224 MVMT).

steps.title: Prepare data for MATLAB
steps.instruction: Transpose each dataset to MATLAB’s column‑major format and save the transposed array as a .mat file named with the participant‑specific identifier.

steps.title: Raw signal examination (Phase A)
steps.instruction: Preprocess and segment the raw OpenBCI EEG data using the OpenBCI software tools as described for Phase A of the EEG‑cleanse pipeline.

steps.title: Data cleaning (Phase B)
steps.instruction: Apply the multi‑stage cleaning workflow in EEGLAB (MATLAB) as follows:

substeps.instruction: Remove high‑impedance channels (retained 407 channels, 58.67 % of the original 4896 channels).
Remove flatline, low‑correlation, and noisy channels (retained 3520 channels, 71.43 % of the original; after this step 3520 channels remain).

Apply Artifact Subspace Reconstruction (ASR) to the remaining 305 sessions (one session excluded for insufficient clean channels). On average 83.36 % of each session is identified as suitable for the clean reference; 102 sessions are fully clean (no reconstruction); overall 20.97 % of the data is reconstructed.

steps.title: Data labeling via ICA (Phase C)
steps.instruction: Decompose the cleaned EEG data with Independent Component Analysis and classify the resulting components:

substeps.instruction: Run ICA on 290 sessions (15 sessions excluded due to insufficient variance or short duration after cleaning).
Classify ICs and retain brain‑related components (3461 total ICs generated; 2440 brain ICs retained, 70.5 % retention; average ≈5 brain‑related ICs per session).
Exclude the 5 sessions (1.7 %) that yielded no usable brain‑related ICs from the final dataset.

steps.title: Record validation outcomes
steps.instruction: Document the following validation metrics: 306 total sessions (16 electrodes each, 4896 channels); 3520 channels retained after cleaning (71.43 %); ASR clean‑reference proportion 83.36 % and reconstruction proportion 20.97 %; ICA produced 3461 ICs with 2440 brain ICs (70.5 %); average of five brain ICs per session; 5 sessions (1.7 %) excluded after labeling.
